changes.current_line: Built for developers: launch payments fast with our APIs, docs and sandbox.
changes.change: For engineering-led marketplace and platform prospects: "Build it before you buy it. Prototype your own payout flow in our sandbox, scoped to how you pay your people." Proof point, anonymized until approved: one customer's engineer, on her own time, "built a working sitter payment flow over a weekend and showed it at Monday standup." Offer a prototype brief for the prospect's own flow (for example, sitter pay) as an explicit evaluation step.
changes.why: The deal turned on the weekend prototype ("Before that it was a bake-off"; afterward Daniel "stopped saying 'if'"), so a hands-on build in the buyer's own flow is stronger proof than M2's launch-fast claim.

changes.current_line: Customers see an average uplift in authorization rates with Authorization Boost and Adaptive Acceptance.
changes.change: Stop leading with the acceptance-rate slide for marketplace and gig prospects with small average transactions and an engineering-led evaluation. Keep it in reserve for buyers who raise lost revenue from declines.
changes.why: The acceptance-rate slide was presented and met with silence, and the buyer dismissed it outright: "our average booking is 38 dollars, I'm not losing sleep over auth rates."

changes.current_line: Financial infrastructure to grow globally, in every currency.
changes.change: For platform prospects whose engineers maintain their own payout code, open on the upkeep burden: "Payments shouldn't be a team. Stop babysitting payments and get your engineers back on the roadmap." Make multi-currency expansion the second line, not the headline.
changes.why: Expansion set the timing (E1), but the pain was two engineers "more or less full-time just keeping sitter payments working" and a roadmap item pushed three quarters, which the customer described as "We want to stop babysitting this."

changes.current_line: Onboard, verify and pay out to sellers worldwide, in their local currency.
changes.change: For marketplaces that pay individual workers: "Keep your promise to the people you pay. Onboard them, verify them, and get them paid locally." Use the buyer's term for their workers' pay (here, "sitter pay") instead of "payouts" or "sellers". Use "paid by Friday" only after product confirms our setup supports that timing.
changes.why: The marketplace capabilities landed (E17), but the customer's words were "sitter pay" and "paid by Friday", not "payouts", so M11 should frame the capability as a promise kept to the people being paid.
